subject: maths
question: Varun and Raju, working together, can complete a job in 40 hours whereas Varun alone can complete the same job in 50 hours. The number of hours required by Raju to complete the job alone is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If two people complete a task in A hours and one of them takes B hours alone, the time taken by the other person is given by (A × B) ÷ (B − A).

Time required by Raju = (40 × 50) ÷ (50 − 40)

⇒ 2000 ÷ 10 = 200 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 200 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Varun and Raju together = 40 hours

Time taken by Varun alone = 50 hours

Total Work = LCM of 40 and 50 = 200 units

 
 

 **Person**
 **Time (Hours)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Varun + Raju
 40
 200
 5
 
 

 Varun
 50
 4
 
 

⇒ Efficiency of Varun and Raju together = 5 units/hour

⇒ Efficiency of Varun alone = 4 units/hour

⇒ Efficiency of Raju alone = (Varun + Raju) − Varun

⇒ Efficiency of Raju alone = 5 − 4 = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Time taken by Raju = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Raju

⇒ Time taken by Raju = 200 ÷ 1 = 200 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 200 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

This topic follows the same logic as Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (filling), while outlet pipes have negative efficiency (emptying).

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, the work is calculated in cycles of 2 days, where the combined efficiency per cycle is the sum of their individual daily efficiencies.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the amount of total work done. If individuals work for the same duration, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.
